messages.content: The Bothell trip is booked, but the supplier moved Friday's closing session online and it will end at noon. Please compare earlier returns with my current flight and tell me whether changing the hotel at the same time would save anything.

Your current Delta return leaves Seattle at 8:20 p.m. The available earlier nonstops are Delta at 3:40 p.m. for a $96 fare increase and Delta at 5:15 p.m. for $41 more. Where will you take the remote session, and will you still have the rental car?
I will join from the Hilton and keep the rental car until I reach Sea-Tac. Assume I can close the laptop by 12:05. I do not want a tight airport transfer.

The 3:40 departure is too compressed once checkout, the drive, rental-car return, and security are included. The 5:15 departure is workable, with roughly three hours from the end of the meeting to departure. I am rechecking its fare and the hotel terms now.
Also verify whether checking out Friday afternoon instead of later changes the room total or creates an early-departure charge. Do not modify either reservation yet.

The hotel is already reserved through Friday checkout, so leaving at 12:15 or 1:00 p.m. does not remove a room night. The property can extend checkout to 1:00 p.m. at no charge, subject to noting it on the reservation. There is no early-departure penalty and the lodging total remains unchanged.
What is the final difference on the 5:15 flight, and how much earlier would I actually get home?

The 5:15 p.m. Delta nonstop has repriced to a $43 fare difference with no separate change fee. It arrives in San Francisco at 7:29 p.m.; your booked 8:20 p.m. flight arrives at 10:32 p.m. The change gains just over three hours for $43.
That is worthwhile. Change only the flight to 5:15, keep the hotel dates as booked, and add the complimentary 1:00 p.m. checkout note.

The return flight is changed to the 5:15 p.m. Delta nonstop for an additional $43. The hotel dates and total are unchanged, and the reservation now notes complimentary checkout at 1:00 p.m. on Friday. No other part of the Bothell trip was modified.
